definition_en: to show or see a connection between things; to tell a story or an account; to feel that you understand someone
core_image: 两条看似无关的旧照片被并排放在桌上
scene: 桌上并排摆着两张旧照片，拍摄年份相差很远。 She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
sceneCN: 这里 relate 是「把……联系起来」（第 1 个义项：看出或说明事物之间的关联）；句意为她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。画面里可留意：并排的旧照片、上面的年份。

senses.title: To see a connection
senses.definition: to show or understand how two things are connected
senses.definitionCN: 说明或理解两件事如何关联
senses.example: She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
senses.exampleCN: 她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to carry back, and a connection is made when one fact is carried back to another and set beside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「带回」，而关联正是在把一个事实带回另一个事实、并排放置时形成的。

senses.title: To tell an account
senses.definition: to give an account of events in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面叙述事件的经过
senses.example: He related the whole journey as if it had happened to someone else.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲述整段旅程，仿佛那是发生在别人身上的事。
senses.why: Telling is also a carrying back: the events are brought from memory into the present and handed to a listener.
senses.whyCN: 讲述同样是「带回」：事件从记忆被带到现在，交到听者手里。

senses.title: To feel understood
senses.definition: to feel that you share an experience with someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 感到自己与某人或某物有共同的经历
senses.example: Teenagers relate to songs that name exactly what they feel.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年会对那些准确说出他们感受的歌产生共鸣。
senses.why: When a story is carried back into your own life, you relate to it; the connection is now inside you.
senses.whyCN: 当一个故事被带回你自己的生活，你就对它产生共鸣；此时这条联系在你心里。

intro.en: Relate belongs to the Latin verb to carry: the same stem that gives refer and reference also gives relation and relative.
intro.cn: relate 属于拉丁语表「携带」的动词：给出 refer 与 reference 的同一词干，也给出 relation 与 relative。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bear, and it underlies a whole family of verbs of transfer.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带或承载，是整族表转移的动词的基础。

items.en: Referre joined re-, back, with ferre and meant to carry back or report.
items.cn: referre 由 re-（往回）与 ferre 组成，意为带回或报告。

items.en: The supine relatus, carried back, supplied the stem rel- to the later verbs and nouns.
items.cn: 动名词形式 relatus（被带回的）为后来的动词与名词提供了 rel- 词干。

items.en: French relater meant to recount or tell, and English took the verb in that sense first.
items.cn: 法语 relater 意为叙述或讲述，英语先以这个意义借入动词。

items.en: The sense of connecting two things grew from the idea of setting one account beside another.
items.cn: 「把两件事联系起来」这一义，由「把一份叙述放在另一份旁边」的观念发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same carrying family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of connecting and recounting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词族的词；近义组收表示联系与叙述的动词。

entries.definition: To carry meaning into another language.
To tell the details of an event.

normalIntro.en: The word carries one thing back to another: two facts side by side, a story to a listener, or a song to your own life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把一物带回另一物：两个事实并排，一个故事交给听者，或一首歌带回你自己的生活。

normal.en: Re plus late, back plus carried: to carry one thing back to another.
normal.cn: re 加 late（携带）：把一物带回另一物。

normal.en: Relate to a subject means to see yourself in it.
normal.cn: relate to 一个话题，指在其中看到自己。

normal.en: Be related to can mean connected by blood or by cause.
normal.cn: be related to 既可指有血缘，也可指有因果。

normal.en: To relate a story is to tell it from beginning to end.
normal.cn: relate a story 指从头到尾讲述它。

normal.en: Relation, relationship, and relative all come from the same carried stem.
normal.cn: relation、relationship、relative 都出自同一个「携带」词干。

abstract.en: To relate is to refuse to let a fact stand alone.
abstract.cn: 联系，就是不让一个事实孤立地站着。

abstract.en: We relate to stories that carry our own lives back to us.
abstract.cn: 我们与那些把我们自己的生活带回给我们的故事共鸣。

abstract.en: A mind that relates well is a mind with many bridges.
abstract.cn: 善于联系的心，是一座桥很多的城。

examples.en: She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
examples.cn: 她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。

examples.en: He related the whole journey as if it had happened to someone else.
examples.cn: 他讲述整段旅程，仿佛那是发生在别人身上的事。

examples.en: Teenagers relate to songs that name exactly what they feel.
examples.cn: 青少年会对那些准确说出他们感受的歌产生共鸣。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 late（带）：把一个事实带回另一个事实，是联系；把经历带回来讲，是讲述；把故事带回自己身上，是共鸣。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回、报告）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 法语 relater（叙述）→ 英语 relate；同族有 relation、relationship、relative、relatively，形近的 refer、reference 也出 ferre。

sensesIntro.en: The core is carrying one thing back to another; the senses move from a link between facts, to a story told, to a story felt as one's own.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把一物带回另一物」；义项从事实之间的关联，到讲出的故事，再到被当作自身经历的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two old photographs laid side by side on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条看似无关的旧照片被并排放在桌上。

branches.en: two dates that explain each other
a journey told to a listener
a song that names your feeling

branches.cn: 被连接的事实与被叙述的事件

branches.en: a story heard and a story lived
branches.cn: 听到的故事与亲历的故事

intro.en: The Latin verb of carrying takes a prefix of return, and its stem then grows a family of nouns about connection and kinship.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「携带」动词接上表返回的前缀，其词干随后长出整族表联系与亲属的名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is ferre, to carry; re- means back, and relatus supplies the stem rel- for relate and relation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 ferre（携带）；re- 表「往回」，relatus 提供 relate 与 relation 的 rel- 词干。

definition_zh: 楼梯的一级；台阶（常用复数指整段楼梯）
definition_en: one step in a set of steps for going up or down between levels, usually used in the plural to mean a staircase
core_image: 一级一级往上的踏板——每一级都把人抬高一点
scene: 老宅的楼梯在脚下吱吱作响。 He counted every stair as he climbed to the attic.
sceneCN: 这里 stair 是「楼梯的一级」（第 1 个义项：上下楼的单个踏步）；句意为他上阁楼时一级一级数着台阶。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 case 构成，义为「楼梯（整体结构）」
由本词加 way 构成，义为「楼梯通道」
由本词加 well 构成，义为「楼梯井」

senses.title: One step of a staircase
senses.definition: a single horizontal step for climbing between two levels
senses.definitionCN: 在两个高度之间攀爬的单个踏步
senses.example: The third stair from the bottom creaks.
senses.exampleCN: 从下面数第三级会吱嘎响。
senses.why: Each board lifts the foot one small height at a time.
senses.whyCN: 每块踏板一次把脚抬高一小段。

senses.title: The whole set of steps
senses.definition: in the plural, the full series of steps connecting two floors
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式指连接两层楼的整段梯级
senses.example: The children raced down the stairs to breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们跑下楼梯去吃早饭。
senses.why: One step after another becomes the whole ladder of the house.
senses.whyCN: 一级接一级便构成房子里整条登高的梯。

senses.title: Levels of rank or progress
senses.definition: a figurative level in rising through rank or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 比喻职位或成就逐步上升中的一层
senses.example: This job is the first stair to a bigger career.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作是通向更大事业的第一级。
senses.why: Rising in life climbs as the foot does: one level at a time.
senses.whyCN: 人生攀升与脚步一样：一次一层。

senses.title: A hidden or private way
senses.definition: in back stairs, a private or secret route, also for secret influence
senses.definitionCN: back stairs 指不公开的通道，也指暗中影响
senses.example: The servants used the back stairs to stay unseen.
senses.exampleCN: 仆人们走后楼梯以不被人看见。
senses.why: Steps hidden at the back of a house let people move unseen.
senses.whyCN: 藏在宅后的梯级让人不被察觉地走动。

intro.en: Stair is a pure Germanic climbing word: it always meant the board that lifts your foot, nothing more.
intro.cn: stair 是纯粹的日耳曼「攀爬」词：它始终只指抬起脚步的踏板。

items.en: A root meaning "to climb, stride" is generally reconstructed; deeper detail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为词根表示「攀爬、迈步」；更深细节来源不确定。

items.en: Germanic formed words for climbing and stepping, kin to stile.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形成攀爬与迈步之词，与 stile（梯磴）同亲。

items.en: Old English stæger meant a step or ladder for climbing.
items.cn: 古英语 stæger 指攀爬用的踏步或梯子。

items.en: The plural stairs became the usual way to speak of the whole staircase.
items.cn: 复数 stairs 渐成指称整段楼梯的常用说法。

items.en: Compounds like staircase and stairwell fixed the family in modern buildings.
items.cn: staircase、stairwell 等复合词使该词族固定于现代建筑。

note.en: Stair heads a building family and sounds like the unrelated stare.
note.cn: stair 领衔建筑词族，且与不相关的 stare 发音相同。

entries.definition: to look at something long and fixedly
entries.definitionCN: 凝视；与 stair 同音但词源不同

entries.definition: steps for crossing a fence, same Germanic root

entries.definitionCN: 楼梯整体；由 stair 加 case 构成

entries.definition: one movement or surface of walking
two rails with rungs for climbing
entries.definitionCN: 梯子；可移动的攀爬工具

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks for stair and its family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条真实钩子帮助记住 stair。

normal.en: stair sounds like stare: climb, don't just look.
normal.cn: stair 与 stare 同音：要攀爬，别只是盯着看。

normal.en: staircase = stair + case, the boxed whole of the steps.
normal.cn: staircase = stair + case，装着梯级的「盒」。

normal.en: a flight of stairs: one connected run of climbing.
normal.cn: a flight of stairs：一整段相连的攀爬。

normal.en: back stairs: the hidden steps behind the grand front ones.
normal.cn: back stairs：气派前梯背后的暗梯。

normal.en: stairwell is the open shaft the stairs spiral around.
normal.cn: stairwell 是楼梯盘旋其中的竖井。

abstract.en: Feel each board rise under your shoe, one by one.
abstract.cn: 感受鞋底之下一级一级抬起的踏板。

abstract.en: Hear the creak of the third step every single time.
abstract.cn: 每次都听见第三级的吱嘎声。

abstract.en: See the top stair appear like a horizon you reach.
abstract.cn: 看见最上一级如可抵达的地平线般浮现。

examples.en: She swept every stair from the cellar to the attic.
examples.cn: 她把从地窖到阁楼的每级台阶都扫了一遍。

examples.en: A flight of stone stairs led up to the tower gate.
examples.cn: 一段石阶通向塔楼大门。

examples.en: Promotion came one stair at a time, never two.
examples.cn: 晋升一级一级来，从不连跳两级。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯黛尔」——像「斯台儿」：一小小的台阶儿，斯斯文文一级级往上。

root: 古英语 stæger「踏步、梯」，属日耳曼语源，与 stile 同亲；一般认为出自表示「攀爬、迈步」的印欧词根，确切形式来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Stair keeps one image: the single board that lifts the foot, which the plural stretches into the whole climb.
sensesIntro.cn: stair 只有一个意象：抬起脚步的单块踏板；复数把它拉成整段攀爬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one board that lifts the foot upward
core.cn: 核心意象：把脚向上抬起的一块踏板

branches.en: the single step and the whole series

branches.cn: 作为日常楼梯的复数用法

intro.en: Stair is a short Germanic word whose family is built with whole-word compounds.
intro.cn: stair 是短小的日耳曼词，其词族以整词复合构成。

latinIntro.en: Stair has no Latin relatives; it never borrowed, it only compounded.
latinIntro.cn: stair 没有拉丁同族词；它从不借词，只做复合。

items.meaning: the framed structure holding the steps
items.example: The spiral staircase fills the tower.
The stairway was blocked by boxes.
Maids carried trays up the back stairs.
items.exampleCN: 女佣端着托盘走上后楼梯。

items.example: Take the up stairs, not the lift.
A red stair-carpet ran the whole flight.
items.exampleCN: 红楼梯地毯铺满整段楼梯。

items.example: Climb the stile to reach the field.
She climbed a flight of stairs daily.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 case 构成，义为「楼梯整体」
由本词加 way 构成，义为「梯道」
由本词加 well 构成，义为「楼梯井」

definition_zh: 摊位；畜栏；熄火；拖延；失速
definition_en: a small enclosed place for an animal, a market stand, or to stop running or delay on purpose
core_image: 一格被围住的小空间——牲口站进去、货摆出来、引擎也卡在这里停下
scene: 集市清晨的木摊架刚搭好。 She bought two baskets of apples at a fruit stall near the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 stall 是「摊位」（第 3 个义项：集市上的售货台）；句意为她在门口附近的水果摊买了两篮苹果。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加-ing 构成，义为「拖延；（机）失速」
由本词加 holder 构成，义为「摊主」

senses.title: A small place where an animal stands
senses.definition: an enclosed space in a barn or stable for one animal
senses.definitionCN: 厩舍中围出的供一头牲口站立的小格
senses.example: Each cow stood calmly in its own stall.
senses.exampleCN: 每头牛安静地站在自己的栏位里。
senses.why: The animal is fixed in one small standing place.
senses.whyCN: 牲口被固定在一处小小的站立之所。

senses.title: A small room or seat divided by walls
senses.definition: a small compartment, as in a bathroom or a church seat
senses.definitionCN: 被隔出的小间，如浴室隔间或教堂座椅
senses.example: The office has three toilet stalls down the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊尽头有三个厕所隔间。
senses.why: One standing place, walled off for a person.
senses.whyCN: 为一个人隔出的站立之所。

senses.title: A stand where goods are sold
senses.definition: a table or open-fronted shop in a market
senses.definitionCN: 市场中的售货台或敞面小店
senses.example: A book stall stood at the corner of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 市场拐角有个书摊。
senses.why: The seller's goods stand fixed in one open box, like animals in a stall.
senses.whyCN: 货品像栏中之兽一样固定在一个敞格内。

senses.title: To stop an engine by sudden braking or wrong gear
senses.definition: to stop an engine suddenly because of wrong gear use or a blocked wheel
senses.definitionCN: 因挡位不当或车轮受阻使发动机突然停转
senses.example: The learner driver stalled at every red light.
senses.exampleCN: 新手司机每个红灯都熄火。
senses.why: The engine is held still, like an animal fixed in its stall.
senses.whyCN: 引擎被卡住不动，如牲口被拴在栏中。

senses.title: To delay on purpose
senses.definition: to delay or hold up an answer, decision, or process deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 故意推迟答复、决定或进程
senses.example: The lawyer stalled for time before the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 律师在开庭前设法拖延时间。
senses.why: Holding something in a fixed place keeps it from moving forward.
senses.whyCN: 把事情按在原地不动，即是拖延。

senses.title: To lose lifting speed in flight
senses.definition: to stop producing lift because the airflow over the wings breaks
senses.definitionCN: 因机翼气流破坏而失去升力
senses.example: The plane stalled and dropped sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机失速急坠。
senses.why: The wings can no longer keep the plane going upward; it falls still.
senses.whyCN: 机翼无法再托起飞机，机身停坠。

intro.en: Stall comes straight from Germanic words for a standing place, the same root family as stable's barn.
intro.cn: stall 直接来自日耳曼语的「站立之所」，与 stable（马厩）同根同族。

items.en: The stand-root, meaning "to stand", underlies the family.
items.cn: 表示「站立」的词根是整个词族的基础。

items.en: Germanic formed stall for a fixed standing place for animals.
items.cn: 日耳曼语以 stall 指牲口的固定站位。

items.en: Old English steall meant a place to stand, a stall, or a seat.
items.cn: 古英语 steall 指站立处、栏位或座位。

items.en: The market stand sense and the church seat sense spread.
items.cn: 集市摊位义与教堂座位义扩展。

items.en: Engine stalling and flight stalling gave the verb its modern force.
items.cn: 熄火与失速赋予动词现代用法。

note.en: Stall shares its standing-place root with stable and store, and sounds close to still.
note.cn: stall 与 stable、store 同享「站立之所」词根，且与 still 音近。

entries.definition: a building for horses, same stand-root
entries.definitionCN: 马厩；与 stall 同源于「站立」词根
静止的；音近但词源不同

entries.definition: a person running a market stall
a small temporary shop or compartment
a small fenced enclosure for animals

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks for stall's two lives.
normalIntro.cn: 五条真实钩子帮助记住 stall 的两副面孔。

normal.en: stall and stable share the stand-root: both are standing places.
normal.cn: stall 与 stable 同根：都是「站立之所」。

normal.en: A market stall is one open box, like one animal stall.
normal.cn: 集市摊位是一个敞格，恰如一个畜栏。

normal.en: stall for time: hold the answer in one place.
normal.cn: stall for time：把答复按在原地。

normal.en: Engine stalls when it cannot keep turning.
normal.cn: 引擎转不动就 stall（熄火）。

normal.en: Planes stall when wings stop lifting.
normal.cn: 机翼失去升力飞机即 stall（失速）。

abstract.en: See one cow in one wooden box, calm and fixed.
abstract.cn: 看见一头牛安静地立在一个木格里。

abstract.en: Watch an apple seller open his wooden box at dawn.
abstract.cn: 看见果贩清晨支起他的木摊。

abstract.en: Feel the car shudder and stop at the lights.
abstract.cn: 感受汽车在红灯前抖动、熄火。

examples.en: The market stall sold fresh fish every Saturday.
examples.cn: 那个集市摊位每周六卖鲜鱼。

examples.en: Don't stall the answer; we need a decision today.
examples.cn: 别拖着不答；我们今天就要决定。

examples.en: He stalled the car twice during the driving test.
examples.cn: 他考驾照时熄火两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯多」——像「死堵」：死死堵在栏里、堵在摊上、堵在路上不动。

root: 古英语 steall「站立处、栏位」，属日耳曼语源，与 stable 同出「站立」词根；该词族演变路径为通常看法。

sensesIntro.en: One standing place becomes a cow's box, a church seat, a market stand, a stopped engine, and a stalling flight.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「站立之所」长成牛栏、教堂座椅、集市摊位、熄火的引擎与失速的航班。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one fixed small standing place that stops movement
core.cn: 核心意象：一个固定的小站位，令运动止息

branches.cn: 供牲口与人隔出的格间

branches.en: goods standing in an open box

branches.cn: 被按住不动的引擎与答复

intro.en: Stall is a short stand-root word; compounds carry its meanings outward.
intro.cn: stall 是短小的「站立」词根词，其诸义靠复合词向外延展。

latinIntro.en: Stall shares Germanic roots with stable and store; no Latin entry applies here.
latinIntro.cn: stall 与 stable、store 共享日耳曼词根；此处无拉丁同族条目。

items.example: The stallholder packed up at dusk.

items.meaning: the act of delaying or losing lift

items.example: Each room has its own shower stall.
items.exampleCN: 每间房都有独立淋浴隔间。

items.example: They sat in the front stalls.

items.meaning: a horse building from the same root

definition_zh: 政治；政治活动；政治见解；政界；政治学；组织内部的权术运作
definition_en: the activity by which people govern, compete for office and settle collective decisions, also used for a person's views, the profession, the academic subject and internal manoeuvring
core_image: 旱季的村口，两派人围在水渠分水口争论，最后按人头重新排定用水次序
scene: 旱季的村口，两派人围在水渠的分水口争论，最后按人头重新排定用水次序。 Politics in the valley had always been about who controlled the water.
sceneCN: 这里指「治理与争夺权力的活动」，对应第 1 个义项：围绕公共资源由谁决定而展开的争夺；句意为这条山谷里的政治历来就是围绕谁掌握水源展开的。画面要点：分水口、两排站立的人、记名的木板；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The activity of governing and competing for power
senses.titleCN: 治理与争夺权力的活动
senses.definition: the activity by which groups decide who holds public authority and how it is used
senses.definitionCN: 各群体决定公共权力归谁掌握、如何使用的活动
senses.example: Politics decides who gets the water and who waits.
senses.exampleCN: 政治决定谁能先得水、谁只能等。
senses.why: the Greek root names the city and its citizens, so the word began as the business of the civic body rather than of private life.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的希腊词根指城邦及其公民，因此它最初指公民集体的事务，而非私人生活。

senses.title: A person's views or affiliation
senses.titleCN: 个人的政治见解或党派立场
senses.definition: the set of beliefs a person holds about how society and government should be run
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对社会与政府应如何运转所持的一整套信念
senses.example: Her politics are greener than her party's platform.
senses.exampleCN: 她的政治立场比本党纲领更偏环保。
senses.why: beliefs about governing are held by individuals, so the plural noun came to mean one person's stance and can take a plural verb in this sense.
senses.whyCN: 关于治理的信念由个人持有，因此这个以复数形式收尾的名词转指个人的立场，作此义时可用复数动词。

senses.title: The profession and world of politicians
senses.definition: the career, workplace and daily life of those who hold or seek public office
senses.definitionCN: 担任或谋求公职者的职业、职场与日常处境
senses.example: He went into politics after running the city hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 他管过市立医院之后进入了政界。
senses.why: an activity that occupies a career becomes a place one enters, hence phrases about going into or leaving politics.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动一旦占据一份职业，就变成可以走进去的场所，于是有了进入政界、退出政界这类说法。

senses.title: The academic subject
senses.titleCN: 政治学（学科名，英式常用）
senses.definition: the study of government and political behaviour as a university discipline
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里把政府与政治行为作为研究对象的学科
senses.example: She read politics before turning to law.
senses.exampleCN: 她先读政治学，之后转行学法。
senses.why: the Greek title of a book on civic affairs became the name of the school subject that studies them.
senses.whyCN: 一本论城邦事务的希腊书名，后来成了研究这些事务的学科名称。

senses.title: Manoeuvring inside an organization
senses.definition: the informal struggle for influence and favour within a workplace, club or family
senses.definitionCN: 在工作场所、团体或家庭内部为影响力与青睐而进行的非正式争夺
senses.example: Office politics kept the best engineer off the project.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里的权术让最好的工程师进不了这个项目。
senses.why: the patterns of alliance and rivalry repeat at any scale, so the word is borrowed wherever a small group allocates scarce goods.
senses.whyCN: 结盟与对立的方式在任何规模上都会重演，因此只要小群体分配稀缺之物，这个词就会被借去用。

senses.title: Public contest over policy and office
senses.titleCN: 围绕政策与职位的公共竞争
senses.definition: the open competition of parties, campaigns and interest groups over what government should do
senses.definitionCN: 政党、竞选活动与利益团体围绕政府应当做什么而展开的公开竞争
senses.example: The politics of the budget turned on two marginal seats.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的政治角力集中在两个边缘选区上。
senses.why: when conflict is public and organised, the word names the contest itself rather than the general activity.
senses.whyCN: 当冲突公开且有组织时，这个词指的是竞争本身，而不是笼统的活动。

senses.title: The arena or system as a whole
senses.titleCN: 政治舞台与制度环境的总称
senses.definition: the whole institutional setting in which authority is won, used and lost
senses.definitionCN: 权力被赢得、使用与失去的整套制度环境
senses.example: Trust in politics fell after the expenses scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 报销丑闻之后，人们对政治这一套制度的信任下降了。
senses.why: the activity and the setting are named by one word, so the noun can stand for the entire arena in which the activity happens.
senses.whyCN: 活动与场所用同一个词表示，因此这个名词也能指活动发生的整个场域。

senses.title: Abstract: the negotiation of collective interests
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：集体利益的协商过程
senses.definition: in general use, any process by which a group with diverging interests reaches a workable decision
senses.definitionCN: 泛指利益分歧的群体达成可行决定的任何过程
senses.example: There is politics in every committee that must divide a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 凡是要分预算的委员会，都有政治。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps only the settling of divergent interests and lets the state and the ballot drop away.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只留下「摆平分歧利益」这层意思，国家与选票则退出了画面。

intro.en: Politics goes back through French and Latin to the Greek title of Aristotle's book on civic affairs, built on the Greek word for a city. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: politics 经法语与拉丁语上溯到亚里士多德论城邦事务那本书的希腊书名，其词根是希腊语中表示「城邦」的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis meant a city-state and the citizen body that made it; its deeper origin is not established, and the suggestion of a pre-Greek source is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: polis 指城邦以及构成城邦的公民总体；它更深的来源未得到证明，关于其源自前希腊语层的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Polites meant a citizen, one who belongs to the polis and shares in its decisions, and from it came the adjective politikos 'of citizens, civic'.
items.cn: politēs 指公民，即属于城邦并参与其决定的人；由它产生形容词 politikos「公民的、城邦的」。

items.en: Ta politika meant 'the things concerning the city', the title of Aristotle's treatise on the government of states, and it named civic affairs rather than party strife.
items.cn: ta politika 意为「与城邦有关的事务」，是亚里士多德论国家治理那部书的书名，所指为公民事务，而非党派争斗。

items.en: Medieval Latin politica was coined from the Greek title to name the study of the state, and it passed through French into English in the late fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 politica 依那个希腊书名造出，用来指对国家的研究，并在十五世纪晚期经法语进入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word spread to party competition, then to the internal manoeuvring of any institution, and finally to 'the politics of' almost any activity.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词先扩展到党派竞争，再指任何机构内部的权术，最后出现「某事背后的政治」这种几乎可用于一切活动的说法。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Greek city root that are easily confused with politics; group two holds terms for governing that do not carry the competitive sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「城邦」词根、容易与 politics 混淆的词；第二组是表示治理、但不含竞争意味的术语。

entries.definition: A settled course of action adopted by a government or firm; politics is the struggle that produces or blocks a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 政府或机构采用的既定行动方案；政治则是产生或阻挠某项政策的那场争夺。

entries.definition: A politically organised society viewed as a unit, as in a federal polity; it names the body, not its activity.
entries.definitionCN: 被视作一个单位的有政治组织的社会，如联邦政体；它指共同体本身，而非其活动。

entries.definition: An older adjective meaning shrewd and tactful, as in a politic silence; it describes judgement, not government.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词，意为精明得体的，如得体的沉默；它描述判断力，而非政府事务。

entries.definition: A person who holds or seeks office; the practice they live by is politics, and the two are constantly used together.
entries.definitionCN: 担任或谋求公职的人；他们以此谋生的活动就是政治，两者常连用。

entries.definition: The body that exercises authority in a state; government is the machine, while politics is the contest that drives it.
entries.definitionCN: 在国家中行使权力的机构；政府是机器，政治则是驱动机器的那场竞争。

entries.definition: The processes and rules by which decisions are taken, often used of firms and agencies; it is quieter and more technical than politics.
entries.definitionCN: 作出决定所依的流程与规则，常用于企业与机构；它比政治更平实、更技术化。

entries.definition: The art of conducting state affairs, especially foreign policy; it stresses skill and is used of leaders rather than of voters.
entries.definitionCN: 处理国家事务、尤其外交事务的技艺；强调技巧，多用于领导人而非选民。

entries.definition: A neutral term for matters of common concern and the work of dealing with them; it avoids the combative tone of politics.
entries.definitionCN: 对公共事务及其处理工作的中性说法；避开了政治一词的争斗意味。

normal.en: The root is the Greek word for a city-state, so politics is literally the business of the city.

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: go into politics, office politics, party politics, the politics of reform.
normal.cn: 固定搭配给各义项分类：进入政界、办公室权术、党派政治、改革的政治角力。

normal.cn: 这个词虽以表示复数的词尾结尾，但指活动或学科时作单数用。

normal.en: A politician lives by politics; a policy is what the struggle produces.
normal.cn: 政治家靠政治为生；政策则是这场争夺的产物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「城邦的事务」——城里人一起商量谁说了算 → 政治

root: politics 经法语与拉丁语出自希腊 ta politika「与城邦有关的事务」，源头是 polis「城邦」与 politēs「公民」；polis 更深来源不确定，前希腊语来源仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses widen from one root: the business of the city becomes a career, then a set of personal beliefs, a university subject, the manoeuvring of any small group, an open electoral contest, the whole arena, and finally any settlement of divergent interests.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一个词根向外扩：城邦的事务先成为一门职业，再成为个人的一整套信念、一门大学学科、任何小团体内部的权术、公开的选举竞争、整个政治场域，最后是任何摆平分歧利益的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: neighbours arguing at a water gate until a rule is agreed.
core.cn: 核心意象：邻人在分水口争论，直到商定一条规则。

branches.en: ROOT ACTIVITY: deciding who holds public authority, the oldest and widest reading.
branches.cn: 根本活动：决定公共权力归谁，这是最古老也最宽的读法。

branches.en: PERSONAL AND PROFESSIONAL: the same word covers what a private person believes and the trade a public person lives by.
branches.cn: 个人与职业：同一个词既指私人的信念，也指公开人物赖以谋生的行业。

branches.en: SUBJECT: the civic business turned into a course of study with its own methods.
branches.cn: 学科：城邦事务被变成一门有自身方法的研究。

branches.en: SCALE OF CONFLICT: quiet manoeuvring in an office and open contest at an election are the same pattern at different sizes.
branches.cn: 冲突的规模：办公室里无声的权术与选举中公开的竞争，是同一种格局的不同尺寸。

branches.en: ARENA AND GENERAL FORM: the whole stage where authority changes hands, then any group dividing what it needs.
branches.cn: 场域与一般形态：先是权力易手的整个舞台，后是任何分配所需之物的群体。

intro.en: Politics rests on a Greek noun for the city and its citizen body, a stem that also builds policy, polity and politician in English.
intro.cn: politics 立在一个表示城邦及其公民总体的希腊名词上，同一词干在英语里还造出政策、政体与政治家。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek stem as politicus and politica, the forms through which the word family reached English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词干借作 politicus 与 politica，这个词族正是经这两种形式进入英语的。

items.example: The root names the unit within which decisions were made.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指出作出决定的那个单位。

items.example: The citizen, not the subject, is the base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的基础是公民，而非臣民。

items.example: The adjective described matters that concerned the citizen body.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述与公民总体相关的事务。

items.structure: -ics (Greek suffix naming an art or study)
items.example: The suffix turns civic affairs into a named field.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把城邦事务变成一个有名称的领域。

items.structure: Old French policie, from Latin politica
items.example: Policy is the settled plan, not the contest.
items.exampleCN: 政策是定下来的方案，而非争夺本身。

items.example: A polity can be a city, a state or a federation.
items.exampleCN: 政体可以是一座城、一个国家或一个联邦。

items.example: The budget dispute politicized the school board.
items.exampleCN: 预算争执把校董会政治化了。

items.example: The decision was political rather than technical.
items.exampleCN: 这个决定是政治性的，而非技术性的。

latinEntries.structure: politicus, politica, politicum (adjective, borrowed from Greek)
politica, politicae (f., first declension; from Greek ta politika)
politia, politiae (f., first declension; from Greek politeia)

definition_zh: 转变；转换；换算；使改变信仰；皈依者
definition_en: to change something into another form or use, or a person who has adopted a new belief
core_image: 一只旧木箱被拆开，重新钉成一张书桌
scene: 老仓库空了许多年，如今门口挂上了书店的牌子。 They plan to convert the warehouse into a bookstore.
sceneCN: 这里 convert 指「改造；转变」（第 1 个义项：把某物改成另一种形态或用途）；句意是他们打算把仓库改造成书店。

pos.zh: 转变；转换；换算；使改变信仰

collocations.zh: 把 A 转变成 B

collocations.phrase: a convert to the new method

senses.title: To change form or use
senses.definition: to change something so that it takes a different form or serves a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物，使其呈现另一种形态或有了新用途
senses.example: The barn was converted into a house.
senses.exampleCN: 这座谷仓被改造成了住宅。
senses.why: The same material can serve twice if the shape is changed.
senses.whyCN: 同样的材料，只要改变形状，就能再用一次。

senses.title: To change units or money
senses.definition: to change a value from one system or currency into another
senses.definitionCN: 把数值从一种体系或货币换成另一种
senses.example: You can convert pounds into dollars here.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以在这里把英镑换成美元。
senses.why: Two languages of counting need a bridge, and this verb is that bridge.
senses.whyCN: 两套计数语言之间需要桥，这个动词就是那座桥。

senses.title: A person who has changed belief
senses.definition: someone who has adopted a new religion or set of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 接受了新宗教或新观念的人
senses.example: He became a convert to the new method.
senses.exampleCN: 他转而拥护这种新方法。
senses.why: When a view turns a person around, the person is named after the turn.
senses.whyCN: 当一种看法把一个人转了个方向，人就用这次转向来命名。

intro.en: Convert comes from Latin convertere, to turn about, built from com-, together, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: convert 来自拉丁语 convertere（转过来），由 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, twist or change direction.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动、扭动或改变方向。

items.en: Convertere meant to turn something right round or turn it into another thing.
items.cn: convertere 意为把某物整个转过来，或把它变成另一样东西。

items.en: Conversus, the turned one, described a person or thing changed completely.
items.cn: conversus 指被转过来的人或物，形容彻底改变。

items.en: Old French convertir kept both the physical and the religious senses.
items.cn: 古法语 convertir 同时保留了物理与宗教两种含义。

items.en: English convert first meant to turn from one belief to another.
items.cn: 英语 convert 最初指从一种信仰转向另一种。

items.en: The word now also covers files, fuel and currency.
items.cn: 今天这个词也涵盖文件、燃料与货币的转换。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vert-, and the meaning group names other verbs of change.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vert-，近义组列出其他表示改变的动词。

entries.definition: the act of changing into another form
able to be changed into another form
to change something completely in form
to make something become another thing
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变成另一样东西

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a box turned into a table, then move to money exchanged and to a person turned toward a new belief.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只箱子变成桌子开始，再到货币兑换，最后到一个人转向新的信仰。

normal.en: Con- is together and vert is to turn, so convert is to turn a thing into a new shape.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vert 是转，convert 就是把东西转成一个新样子。

normal.en: Same wood, new table: nothing is lost, only rearranged.
normal.cn: 同样的木头，新的桌子：什么也没少，只是重新排列。

normal.en: A file becomes a picture, a pound becomes a dollar, a sum becomes a score.
normal.cn: 文件变成图片，英镑变成美元，算式变成得分。

normal.en: The noun convert is a person who has made this turn in belief.
normal.cn: 名词 convert 就是在信仰上完成这次转向的人。

normal.en: Remember the stress moves: con-VERT the verb, CON-vert the person.
normal.cn: 记住重音会移动：动词读 con-VERT，指人时读 CON-vert。

abstract.en: Picture a key melted down and recast as a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被熔化，重新铸成戒指。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows curving into one circle.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头弯成一个圆。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp turned from a dark corner to a bright wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯从暗角转向明亮的墙面。

examples.en: They converted the old factory into flats.
examples.cn: 他们把旧工厂改成了公寓。

examples.en: The app can convert your photos into a short film.
examples.cn: 这个应用能把你的照片转成一段短片。

examples.en: He is a recent convert to cycling.
examples.cn: 他最近成了骑行爱好者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convert 记成 con（一起）加 vert（转）：把原样整个转过去，就是转变与换算。

root: 源自拉丁语 convertere（转过来），由 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成，本指转向，后引申为形态转换与信仰改变。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing turned into a new shape, to values exchanged, and at last to a person turned toward a new belief.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一件东西被转成新形态，到数值互换，最后到一个人转向新的信仰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old box taken apart and nailed into a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旧箱子被拆开，钉成一张书桌。

branches.en: A building or object is turned to a new purpose.
branches.cn: 一座建筑或一件物品被转向新的用途。

branches.en: A number or a note changes system without losing worth.
branches.cn: 一个数字或一张钞票换了体系，却不失价值。

branches.en: A person turns, and the turn gives the person a new name.
branches.cn: 一个人转了向，这次转向就给了他一个新的称呼。

branches.en: Both are conversions of form, one physical and one abstract.
branches.cn: 两者都是形态转换，一个具体，一个抽象。

branches.en: Money and belief both change hands and change sides.
branches.cn: 金钱与信仰都会换手，也会换边。

intro.en: Convert is built on Latin com-, together, plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: convert 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 vertere（转）构成。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vert- also runs through reverse, version and versatile.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vert- 也贯穿 reverse、version 与 versatile。

items.meaning: a device that changes one form into another
items.meaningCN: 把一种形态变成另一种的装置
items.exampleCN: 转换器发出轻微的嗡声。

items.meaning: to turn back the other way
a form produced from an original
items.meaningCN: 由原本产生的一种形态

items.meaning: able to turn to many tasks

definition_en: to hit something lightly and suddenly
core_image: 车轮压过石头时车身一颠
scene: 土路上满是碎石。 The old car bumped over the stones.
sceneCN: 这里 bump 是「颠簸」（第 2 个义项：行进中不断碰撞起伏）；句意是旧车在石头上颠簸着开过。

senses.title: To hit something lightly
senses.definition: to hit something by accident, usually not hard
senses.definitionCN: 意外地、通常不重地撞到某物
senses.example: She bumped her knee on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她的膝盖撞到了桌子。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming a dull knock.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指一声闷响的撞击。

senses.title: To move with jolts
senses.definition: to move along over an uneven surface
senses.definitionCN: 在高低不平的表面上行进
senses.example: The old car bumped over the stones.
senses.exampleCN: 旧车在石头上颠簸着开过。
senses.why: A wheel striking each stone repeats the small knock.
senses.whyCN: 车轮碾过每块石头，就是重复一次小小的撞击。

senses.title: A swelling on the skin
senses.definition: a raised area caused by a knock
senses.definitionCN: 撞击后皮肤上鼓起的部分
senses.example: A small bump rose on his forehead.
senses.exampleCN: 他额头上鼓起一个小包。
senses.why: The result of a knock took the name of the knock.
senses.whyCN: 撞击留下的结果沿用了撞击的名字。

intro.en: Bump is an imitative word for a dull blow, then the swelling it leaves.
intro.cn: bump 是模仿闷响撞击的拟声词，后指撞击留下的肿包。

items.en: bump imitated the sound of a heavy knock.
items.cn: bump 模仿沉重撞击的声音。

items.en: The verb named hitting against something.
items.cn: 动词指撞到某物上。

items.en: The noun named the swelling left by a knock.
items.cn: 名词指撞击留下的肿块。

items.en: Bumpy described rough roads and rides.
items.cn: bumpy 形容崎岖的道路与颠簸的行程。

items.en: bump covers a knock, a jolting ride and a lump.
items.cn: 如今 bump 涵盖碰撞、颠簸行程与肿包。

note.en: The look-alike group changes one letter and keeps the -ump ending; the near-meaning group gives blow words.
note.cn: 形近组只换一个字母、保留 -ump 结尾；近义组是撞击类的词。

entries.definition: to hit a door or surface
a raised part on the body

normalIntro.en: Bump sounds exactly like the noise it names.
normalIntro.cn: bump 读起来就像它所指的那声闷响。

normal.en: You bump into a friend by chance.
normal.cn: bump into 指偶然遇到朋友。

normal.en: The plural is bumps.
normal.cn: 复数是 bumps。

normal.en: A bumpy road shakes the whole car.
normal.cn: 崎岖的路让整车都在颠。

normal.en: The bumper takes the first hit.
normal.cn: 保险杠承受第一下撞击。

normal.en: A bump on the head needs a cold cloth.
normal.cn: 头上的肿包要用冷毛巾敷。

abstract.en: See a wheel drop into a hole and climb out.
abstract.cn: 想象车轮陷进坑里又爬出来。

abstract.en: See a knee meeting the corner of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象膝盖撞上桌角。

abstract.en: See a slow swelling above an eyebrow.
abstract.cn: 想象眉毛上方慢慢鼓起的包。

examples.en: The old car bumped over the stones.
examples.cn: 旧车在石头上颠簸着开过。

examples.en: She bumped her knee on the table.
examples.cn: 她的膝盖撞到了桌子。

examples.en: A small bump rose on his forehead.
examples.cn: 他额头上鼓起一个小包。

dict_mnemonic.text: bump 与 pump 只差一个字母，打气时泵一上一下，车身也跟着一下一下地颠。

root: bump 是十六世纪出现的拟声词，模仿沉闷的撞击声；先作动词表示碰撞，再作名词表示撞出的肿包，十九世纪起用于形容颠簸的道路与行程。

sensesIntro.en: A dull knock, the shaking of a rough ride, and the lump left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 一声闷撞、一段颠簸的路程、以及撞出来的包。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car jolting over loose stones.
core.cn: 核心意象：汽车在碎石上颠了一下。

intro.en: Bump takes -y and -er to name rough surfaces and a car part.
intro.cn: bump 加 -y 与 -er 可表示崎岖和汽车部件。

latinIntro.en: The base is imitative English; the Latin items below are related only in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是英语拟声词，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

items.meaning: the bar that takes a hit
a dark mark from a blow

definition_en: the job or series of jobs that a person does over a long period of life
core_image: 一条越跑越宽的跑道，人一直在上面往前
scene: 她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。 She began her career in journalism.
sceneCN: 这里 career 是「职业生涯」（第 1 个义项：长期从事的工作历程）；句意是她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。

derivatives.zh: career 加 -ist 构成，义为「一味追求升迁的人」
career 加 -ism 构成，义为「追逐个人事业成功」

senses.title: The work a person does over years
senses.definition: the profession or occupation that a person follows for much of their life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人一生中大部分时间从事的专业或工作
senses.example: Teaching became his career after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后教书成了他的职业。
senses.why: Career first meant a racecourse, and a working life came to be seen as a course run over years.
senses.whyCN: career 最初指跑道，而人的工作历程被看成一条跑过多年的赛道。

senses.title: The whole course of working life
senses.definition: the whole period of a person's working life, with its progress and changes
senses.definitionCN: 一个人工作生活的整个时期，包括其中的进展与变化
senses.example: Her career spanned three decades and two continents.
senses.exampleCN: 她的生涯横跨三十年、两个大洲。
senses.why: A course has a start and a finish, so career also names the full span rather than one job.
senses.whyCN: 跑道有起点和终点，所以 career 也指整段历程，而不只是某一份工作。

intro.en: Career began as a word for a racetrack, then became the track of a working life.
intro.cn: career 起初指赛马跑道，后来变成「工作人生的跑道」。

items.en: carrus named a wheeled wagon, the source of many words about vehicles and tracks.
items.cn: carrus 指带轮的车，是许多车辆与道路词的来源。

items.en: carriere meant a racecourse or the track on which horses ran.
items.cn: carriere 指赛马场或马匹奔跑的跑道。

items.en: English borrowed career for a racecourse and for a galloping course.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 career，指跑道与疾驰的路线。

items.en: The word shifted from a physical track to the course of a person's public life.
items.cn: 这个词从实体的跑道转指一个人公共生活的历程。

items.en: Today career means the profession itself and the whole span of working life.
items.cn: 今天 career 既指职业本身，也指整个工作生涯。

note.en: Career is a descendant of the wagon word car, and it sits beside other names for work.
note.cn: career 是「马车」一词 car 的后代，同时和别的「工作」名称相邻。

entries.definition: a road vehicle with an engine
entries.definitionCN: 汽车，与 career 同出拉丁语 carrus。

entries.definition: a railway car or a horse-drawn vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 火车车厢或马车，与 career 同根。

entries.definition: a two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses in ancient races
entries.definitionCN: 古代赛车上用的双轮马车，同样源自 carrus。
需要专门训练的职业，最贴近 career 的第一义。

entries.definition: the kind of work a person does
entries.definitionCN: 一个人所从事的工作类别，较正式的用词。
一份具体的有薪职位，时间跨度比 career 短。

normalIntro.en: The racetrack image makes the word easy: a career is the course you run for years.
normalIntro.cn: 跑道的画面让这个词很好记：career 就是你跑了很多年的那条赛道。

normal.en: career comes from carriere, a racecourse, built on the wagon word carrus.
normal.cn: career 来自 carriere（跑道），建立在「马车」一词 carrus 之上。

normal.en: A racecourse has a start and a direction, just like a working life.
normal.cn: 跑道有起点和方向，工作人生也一样。

normal.en: career path and career choice both use the road metaphor directly.
normal.cn: career path 与 career choice 都直接沿用了「道路」这个比喻。

normal.en: The phrase launch a career treats work as a vehicle setting off.
normal.cn: launch a career 把事业看成一辆出发的车。

normal.en: The plural careers covers several people's working lives.
normal.cn: 复数 careers 指多人的职业生涯。

abstract.en: Picture a long track curving out of sight, with footprints already on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的跑道弯出视线，上面已有脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a horse cart on the same track, then a car, then a person walking.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条跑道上先是马车，再是汽车，最后是一个步行的人。

abstract.en: Picture a single line drawn through many years on a calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象在日历上画一条穿过许多年的线。

examples.en: She began her career in journalism.
examples.cn: 她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。

examples.en: Teaching became his career after graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业后教书成了他的职业。

examples.en: Her career spanned three decades and two continents.
examples.cn: 她的生涯横跨三十年、两个大洲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可瑞尔」——在跑道上一直往前跑，就是职业生涯。

root: 拉丁语 carrus（车）→ 古法语 carriere（跑道）→ 英语 career（跑道，后指人生历程）。

sensesIntro.en: One metaphor, two reaches: the profession itself and the whole course it runs on.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个比喻，两种跨度：职业本身，以及它所在的那整条跑道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a racetrack stretching forward, with someone running along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条向前延伸的跑道，有人正在上面奔跑。

branches.en: The job sense: the profession a person settles into.
branches.cn: 工作义：一个人长期从事的职业。

branches.en: The span sense: the whole run from first job to retirement.
branches.cn: 跨度义：从第一份工作到退休的整段历程。

branches.en: Both senses borrow the shape of a track: direction, progress, and distance covered.
branches.cn: 两个义项都借用了跑道的形状：方向、进展和已跑过的距离。

branches.en: career development treats the job as something that can be built stage by stage.
branches.cn: career development 把职业看成可以分阶段搭建的东西。

branches.en: A career can be long or short, smooth or broken, like any course.
branches.cn: 生涯可长可短、可顺可断，就像任何一条跑道。

intro.en: Career is a base noun; the suffix -ist and -ism build its small modern family.
intro.cn: career 是基础名词，后缀 -ist 与 -ism 构成它不大的现代词族。

latinIntro.en: The root goes back to Latin carrus, a wagon, which also gives car and carriage.
latinIntro.cn: 词根可追溯到拉丁语 carrus（车），它也带来 car 与 carriage。

items.example: The school advises students on careers.
items.exampleCN: 学校为学生提供职业指导。

items.meaningCN: 一心追求事业升迁的人
items.example: He was seen as a careerist.
items.exampleCN: 他被看作一个只顾往上爬的人。

items.meaning: the pursuit of personal career success
items.meaningCN: 追逐个人事业成功的作风
items.example: Critics blamed careerism for the decision.
items.exampleCN: 批评者把这一决定归咎于追逐名利。

items.example: Carrus is the root of career.
items.exampleCN: carrus 是 career 的词根。

items.meaning: a railway car or horse-drawn vehicle

items.example: The chariot raced around the track.

definition_en: a long seat, or a strong table used for work
core_image: 公园里被晒暖的木长椅
scene: 午后，一位老人坐在公园的长椅上。 An old man sat on a park bench.
sceneCN: 这里 bench 是「长椅」（第 1 个义项：供多人坐的长条座椅）；句意是一位老人坐在公园的长椅上。

pos.zh: 名词：长椅；工作台；法官席
动词：（体育）把球员换下场

derivatives.zh: 由 work 与 bench 复合，义为「工作台」
由 bench 与 warmer 复合，义为「替补队员」

senses.title: A long seat
senses.definition: a long seat for two or more people
senses.definitionCN: 可供两人以上坐的长条座椅
senses.example: An old man sat on a park bench.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老人坐在公园的长椅上。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, a plain seat made of wood or stone.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指木制或石制的简易长座。

senses.title: A strong work table
senses.definition: a sturdy table for a craftsman or worker
senses.definitionCN: 工匠或工人使用的坚固台面
senses.example: The tools are laid out on the work bench.
senses.exampleCN: 工具摆在工作台上。
senses.why: A long seat and a long table share the same flat shape.
senses.whyCN: 长条座椅与长条桌面共用同一种扁平形状。

senses.title: The seat of a judge
senses.definition: the seat or office of a judge
senses.definitionCN: 法官的座位或职位
senses.example: The lawyer approached the judge's bench.
senses.exampleCN: 律师走向法官席。
senses.why: Official seats were raised platforms, and the name stuck.
senses.whyCN: 官方座位多为高台，这个名字沿用下来。

intro.en: Bench is an old Germanic word for a long seat.
intro.cn: bench 是日耳曼语中表示长座位的古老词。

items.en: benc meant a long seat.
items.cn: benc 意为「长凳」。

items.en: benches stood in halls and gardens.
items.cn: 长凳出现在厅堂和花园里。

items.en: the word named a workman's table.
items.cn: 这个词开始指工匠的工作台。

items.en: the judge's seat was called the bench.
items.cn: 法官的座位被称作 the bench。

items.en: sports also use bench for reserve players.
items.cn: 体育中也用 bench 指替补席。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one sound; the near-meaning group gives other seats.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音；近义组是其他坐具。

entries.definition: the sandy edge of the sea

normalIntro.en: A bench is a long flat thing: a seat, a table or a court seat.
normalIntro.cn: bench 是长而平的东西：长椅、工作台或法官席。

normal.en: The plural is benches, with -es.
normal.cn: 复数是 benches，加 es。

normal.en: A park bench waits under the trees.
normal.cn: 公园长椅在树下等着人坐。

normal.en: A work bench holds tools, not people.
normal.cn: work bench 放工具而不坐人。

normal.en: The bench also means the judge's seat.
normal.cn: the bench 也指法官席。

normal.en: A benched player sits out the game.
normal.cn: 被 benched 的球员只能坐板凳。

abstract.cn: 想象被太阳晒暖的木长椅。

abstract.en: See tools spread on a heavy table.
abstract.cn: 想象工具摊在厚重的台面上。

abstract.en: See a judge looking down from a high seat.
abstract.cn: 想象法官从高座上俯视。

dict_mnemonic.text: bench 与 bank 一样是「长条」，河岸是土的长条，长椅是木的长条。

root: 古英语 benc 意为长凳，与德语 Bank 同源；十六世纪起指工匠工作台，十八世纪起指法官席位，现代又引申为体育替补席。

sensesIntro.en: One flat long shape serves as seat, worktable and judge's place.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种长而平的形状，既是座椅，也是工作台和法官席。

core.cn: 核心意象：被太阳晒暖的木长椅。

intro.en: Bench takes -es, -ed and -ing, and joins work and warmer.
intro.cn: bench 可加 -es、-ed、-ing，也能与 work、warmer 复合。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自日耳曼语。
